summary.principle: Finished, reviewed CONTENT slides — reused, never reinvented. A canonical entry is the single approved rendering of a recurring content slide (About SmartBuild, About smrt-E, a leader bio). PLAN searches here FIRST and reuses before authoring net-new. Unlike layouts/library-v9 (empty layout shapes), these entries carry the ACTUAL words. Not a ceiling: PLAN authors net-new whenever nothing fits — it just never rebuilds content that is already published.
summary.content_hash_algo: sha256:16 — sha256 over JSON-encoded [stripped active planFragment block texts...] + [approved_fact.value or .text...], first 16 hex chars. Identical in engine/ingest_decks.py and engine/reference_search.py (content_hash() helper).

provenance_contract.note: Stamped by PLAN on every REUSED or ADAPTED slide (not on net-new authored slides, which are source='authored' by default). Recorded in this catalog (entry.used_in[]) and in archive.json (slide.used_in[]) — NOT inline in plan.json, whose schema forbids extra slide keys. reference_search.record_reuse() writes it.

shape.ref_id: REF-* if reused from this library, else null
shape.archive_id: archive slide id if reused from the deck archive, else null
shape.canonical: bool — true only for canonical library entries
shape.content_hash: hash of the SOURCE content at reuse time (detects later drift)
shape.deck_title: the deck this was reused into
shape.adapted_note: if reuse='adapted', what changed; else null

summary.planFragment_contract: A full plan.schema.json slide object (slide_uuid, topic, layout{family,shape_tags}, group, continues, content_blocks[], optional image_intent/icon_intent). The entry's own approved_facts[] carry any facts the fragment's fact_refs point at. On reuse PLAN copies the fragment into plan.json, RE-MINTS all uuids (uuids are unique per plan, never shared across decks), and merges the entry's approved_facts into the plan's approved_facts.

planFragment.topic: Know Al can be confidently wrong ("hallucinate")

content_blocks.text: Know Al can be confidently wrong ("hallucinate")

AI gets things wrong and sounds confident doing it. Treat it like an intern’s draft. Your judgment is still the final check. No sensitive datain public tools AI uses what you give it and free versions use it for training. Paid workspaces keep your data private. It can process info, but no one else can “see” it Never let Al make a major call without review AI speeds up tasks but can’t replace judgement, experience or context. It supports your work. It doesn’t substitute for it. Playing it safe: 3 Rules of Smart AI Use
